oneLineDefinition: A field focused on planning, implementing, and controlling the flow of goods, services, information, and resources from origin to final customer.
overview: Logistics & Supply Chain Management deals with how products move from manufacturers to consumers — covering procurement, warehousing, transportation, customs, inventory management, and supply chain optimization. It is a field that combines business management, operations research, and practical industry knowledge. Vietnam's strong position in manufacturing and export makes this a high-demand field domestically. It requires both analytical thinking (for optimization) and practical knowledge of trade operations.
toolsAndTechnologies: Power BI for supply chain analytics
typicalProjects: Design a distribution network for a FMCG company
Optimize warehouse layout and slotting for a 3PL provider
Analyze supply chain disruption risk for a manufacturing client
Model inventory replenishment policies using demand data
Prepare export documentation for an international shipment
requiredSkills: Analytical thinking for cost and process optimization
English for international trade documentation and communication
Understanding of import/export regulations and Incoterms
Attention to detail — errors in logistics have real financial consequences
Negotiation skills for procurement and carrier relationships
suitableFor: Students who enjoy operations, process improvement, and problem-solving in physical systems
Those interested in international trade and Vietnam's role in global supply chains
Students who want a business degree with strong real-world application
People who are organized, detail-oriented, and like working with data
notSuitableFor: Students who want primarily creative or people-facing work
Those who want to avoid operational detail and paperwork
Students who have no interest in manufacturing, trade, or physical product flows
keyTakeaways: Vietnam's manufacturing and export growth makes logistics a high-demand field domestically
ERP and data skills are increasingly required — basic Excel is not enough
The field involves significant English communication, especially in international trade roles
Certifications (FIATA, CILT, APICS CSCP) are valued by employers
cautionNotes: Entry-level logistics roles can involve demanding hours, especially in freight and customs
Salary at entry level is not high — significant growth comes with experience and specialization
The field is being disrupted by automation and AI — graduates with data skills have stronger long-term prospects
marketDemand: High in Vietnam, driven by manufacturing, e-commerce, and Vietnam's growing role in global supply chains. Demand is especially strong in industrial zones and export-oriented industries.
salaryOutlook: Entry-level logistics roles earn 8–14M VND/month. Supply chain analysts and procurement specialists earn 15–25M. Senior supply chain managers at multinational companies can earn 40–80M+.
futureTrend: Automation, AI-driven demand forecasting, and e-commerce growth are reshaping the field. Graduates with data analysis and digital supply chain skills are significantly more competitive.
commonMisconceptions: Logistics and Supply Chain Management are the same thing
Logistics is just about driving trucks and moving boxes — at the management level it is a data-driven, strategic function
Logistics has limited career growth — supply chain management is one of the most senior operations functions in large companies
You do not need English in logistics — international trade and most ERP systems require strong English

faq.question: Is Logistics a good major for job placement in Vietnam?
faq.answer: Yes. Vietnam's manufacturing base and growing e-commerce sector create consistent demand for logistics professionals. Job placement rates are generally good, especially in industrial provinces and for students with English proficiency.

faq.question: Is Logistics mostly office work or field work?
faq.answer: It depends on the role. Operations, warehousing, and freight roles involve more field work, while planning, procurement, and analytics roles are primarily office-based.

faq.question: Do I need strong English for Logistics?
faq.answer: Yes. International trade documents, suppliers, freight partners, and multinational companies often require strong English communication.
